claim: Testing MQTT applications is hard because it requires a deployed broker, and sharing one broker deployment across multiple tests causes interference and flaky results.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's 'never reliable' symptom is consistent with missing/brittle MQTT integration tests; per-test ephemeral brokers are the remedy
scope_conditions: MQTT integration testing generally; vendor blog framing
quoted_support: When testing MQTT client applications, you need a deployed MQTT broker. But sharing the deployment across multiple tests can cause unwanted interference between them and produce unexpected results and flaky tests.

claim: Testcontainers mitigates flaky broker tests by automatically creating per-container port mappings to avoid port collisions and deleting all containers after tests to conserve resources.
stance_target: Testcontainers is the right primitive for reliable, parallel-safe MQTT broker tests for ha-linux-agent
quoted_support: Testcontainers also automatically creates port-mapping for each container to mitigate the risk of port-collisions and other interference. After the tests are executed, Testcontainers deletes all containers, to conserve resources.

claim: For ephemeral test setups, broker disk persistence is pointless — HiveMQ's module pre-configures in-memory persistence and adds lifecycle management to guarantee the broker is up before tests execute.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's Mosquitto test container should be configured for ephemeral in-memory operation with explicit readiness gating
scope_conditions: HiveMQ module; pattern transfers to Mosquitto configuration
quoted_support: HiveMQ specific lifecycle management to make sure that HiveMQ and all HiveMQ extensions are up and running before tests are executed ... HiveMQ is pre-configured with in-memory persistence as disk-persistence is not required for ephemeral test-setups.
